title: cloud half of the MCP phase-2 epic: the pricing cell for the open draft entry (D1), and four changes to the hosted MCP build door
body:
epic:#34659#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjMnXJdSZifpEN5i7aU

Filing gate: ④ a child of the cross-repo parent #34659 (the 「MCP 二期与问数」 epic), filed on the maintainer's word in this seat's chat, 2026-11-17, verbatim: 「同意你的所有建议，开始立专题子卡」. The ruling record is #34659 comment 6940528935. Every change here is in the `cloud` repository, so the whole card is the cloud PM's; the epic seat files it here only to hand it over, and asks triage for the routing.

## Why

The maintainer ruled that open source gets the MCP draft write entry (D1 = A) and that rule content is open, enforced first (E1 = A). Both have a cloud side: one line of the pricing table, and the hosted door's own rule corpus. Separately, measuring the hosted door found two defects and a cost nobody had counted.

Who acts: the cloud PM and its lane. Who reads the result: a developer who connects their own AI client to a hosted environment to build.

## Evidence (cloud `53a5844`; the package's own code run against a mocked kernel; the no-argument answer is byte-identical through the real door `execute()`)

- Door tool list: 19 tools, 35,725 bytes. `apply_edit`, `create_object`, `add_field` and `modify_field` are 60% of it.
- `initialize` instructions: 11,580 bytes. First `get_authoring_rules` answer with no arguments: 33,014 bytes.
- Rule corpus: 60 rules. 44 are static text (77,734 characters); 16 depend on the environment (77,221). Of the on-demand text, 40,880 characters are already read from the published `@objectstack/skills`.
- The inline rule `confirm-before-change` has no MCP rendering: the no-argument answer describes the in-product confirm card and `changes_proposed`, and the `solution_design` text in the same answer says the connection has no confirm card.
- The post-apply verification bound and the read de-duplication are keyed on a chat turn id, which the door does not have (`post-apply-verification.ts:427-432`).
- The daily authoring-write cap is an in-memory counter per process (`objectos-runtime/src/mcp-build-volume.ts`).
- `docs/design/pricing.md:113` lists MCP build in the open-source column as "— source mode".
- No build-accuracy eval drives the MCP door; the scenario driver drives the in-app build chat.

## Scope

1. D1: the pricing table's open-source cell for MCP build names the draft write entry; the ADR-0025 / ADR-0082 wording follows.
2. Give `confirm-before-change` an MCP rendering, so the door stops describing a card it does not show.
3. Move static rule text to the published skills as it stabilises (E1), until the served corpus is the environment delta: the restriction profile, the hosted-only rules and the tool-behaviour notes. A rule whose breach is runtime-dead metadata becomes a publish-time check in the framework first; those framework cards are the epic's later milestone, not this card.
4. Make the two turn-keyed guards and the daily cap hold on the door.
5. Measure the door: the byte weights above, kept as a baseline, and a build eval over MCP.

## Out of scope

- The tools themselves stay. The hosted door is not reduced to a draft entry: defaults, tier refusals, confirmation, quotas and `verify_build`'s probes are the hosted product.

## Relations

- Parent: #34659. Design: `docs/design/mcp-local-first-door.md` (PR #34675), Design D.
- Dedup, open and closed, objectstack: `MCP draft authoring tools open-source` 1 hit, the parent. The cloud repository's own backlog was not searched by this seat; the cloud PM dedups there.
